```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Fit to a one-person, agent-run company: B is pure software. The brief says a vision model plus Admin API write-back is narrow and provable, and at least six live competitors, several built by tiny teams, already ship it. A depends on physical fulfillment. Its own brief flags customs, address changes, damaged goods and returns as high-touch work that needs a support team.",
    "Proof that people pay: B's category has published paid tiers. Examples are Describly at $12.90/mo, Gelo.ai at $49.90–$129/mo, Fyvello at $29.99–$59.99/mo and AltText.ai at $5–$59/mo. The leading app has 473 reviews at 4.9 stars, though that one has a free plan. A's pricing anchor, SwagUp at $99–$999/mo, shows payment exists, but it goes to incumbents that already offer the exact Stripe/Zapier-triggered mechanic.",
    "A's core wedge is undercut by its own evidence. The Hampton case shows buyers can already wire Stripe or Zapier to SwagUp themselves. Sendoso connects to Stripe via Tray.io/Pipedream, and Z-Swag explicitly targets SaaS onboarding kits. That leaves A as a reseller layer with no stated differentiator.",
    "Unit economics favor B. The brief cites 0% Shopify revenue share under $1M/year and pennies-per-call inference, so a handful of subscribers can be profitable. A's open questions admit that per-package cost at low volume, and fit for low-ACV customers given $60–$220 kits, are unresolved.",
    "Both face saturation, but B's path to a single paying customer is lower-friction. The listing sits where merchants shop, and Shopify handles billing. A requires either Stripe app review or outbound B2B selling of a physical service against direct incumbents."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence comes entirely from vendor-published customer stories: SwagUp's BurnRate story, the Printfection/Endcrawl case study, and Hampton's existing SwagUp+Zapier workflow. Each describes pain that an incumbent has already solved, not unmet demand a new entrant could capture. Several supporting claims also lack sources. The 'real customs breakdown' has no citation, the $60–$220 kit cost figure cites Merchloop/PerkUp with no URL, and Stitchi/Swag.com pricing was not found.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets where incumbents already deliver the core mechanic. B's own evidence is weak on discovery and on paid demand. The dominant app is free, the ads benchmark implies about $500/mo for 90 days before any signal, there is a 470-review ranking gap, and ARPU is compressed to $5–$13/mo. B wins mainly because its operating model suits a solo AI-run company and A's does not, not because B's demand evidence is clearly stronger."
}
```
